mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an easing monetary policy stance that reduces the discount rate for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the months where FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.0% in the most recent month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the months where UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in consumer credit (RSAFS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a weakening demand environment that triggers a negative feedback loop in equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between RSAFS decline and UNRATE rise does not produce negative returns in more than 60% of the instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of rising industrial production (INDPRO > 105.0), the economy is in an early-cycle expansion phase where corporate profits are growing, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the months where INDPRO exceeds 105.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction (HOUST) over the past two months signals strong housing market activity that boosts consumer confidence and corporate investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the months where HOUST increases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% in the most recent month, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the months where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate indicates a dual stress on monetary policy and labor markets, which triggers a negative equity market reaction, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint rise in FEDFUNDS and UNRATE does not produce negative returns in more than 60% of the instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high labor market slack (UNRATE > 4.5%), the economy is in a recovery phase where corporate hiring is accelerating, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the months where UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.
